title: The derived category of a ringed site is closed symmetric monoidal
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site whose underlying category is small and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Use the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and its unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $K,L\in D(\mathcal O)$ let $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}L$ be represented by the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] of a K-flat complex [def-pc-kflat-complex] representing $K$ and any complex representing $L$, and let $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(L,M)$ be the derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].

Then $D(\mathcal O)$ with tensor bifunctor $\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}$, unit $\mathcal O$ placed in degree zero, the associativity and unit isomorphisms induced on total tensor complexes of K-flat representatives by those of tensor products of module sheaves, and the symmetry $\sigma_{K,L}:K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}L\xrightarrow{\sim}L\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}K$ induced by $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ on the summand of bidegree $(p,q)$, is a monoidal category [def-sfb-monoidal-category] whose symmetry is natural in both variables and satisfies $\sigma_{L,K}\circ\sigma_{K,L}=1$ and the hexagon identity
$$\alpha_{L,M,K}\circ\sigma_{K,L\otimes M}\circ\alpha_{K,L,M}=(1_L\otimes\sigma_{K,M})\circ\alpha_{L,K,M}\circ(\sigma_{K,L}\otimes1_M),$$
where $\alpha_{X,Y,Z}:(X\otimes Y)\otimes Z\xrightarrow{\sim}X\otimes(Y\otimes Z)$ is the associator. It is closed: for all $K,L,M\in D(\mathcal O)$ there is a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}L,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(K,R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(L,M)),$$
natural in $K$, $L$ and $M$ (contravariantly in $K$ and $L$). Its counit at $K=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(L,M)$ is the evaluation $e_{L,M}:R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(L,M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}L\to M$, and a morphism $u:K\to R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(L,M)$ corresponds to $e_{L,M}\circ(u\otimes1_L)$.

source.place: Tag 0FPT (sites-cohomology-lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived: D(O) is symmetric monoidal with the usual associativity and commutativity constraints, signs as in More on Algebra section-sign-rules; proof omitted in the source) and Tag 08J9 (sites-cohomology-lemma-internal-hom: RHom(K,RHom(L,M)) = RHom(K tensor^L L, M), recovering equation-internal-hom Hom(K,RHom(L,M)) = Hom(K tensor^L L, M) on H^0).

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ and write $T(P,N)=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_{\mathcal O}N)$. By [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], sheaf tensor is additive, symmetric monoidal and closed; by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], $\mathcal A$ is Grothendieck and has all small colimits. Tensor preserves colimits: for fixed $F$, the adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(F\otimes\operatorname{colim}G_i,H)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{colim}G_i,\mathcal Hom(F,H))=\lim_i\operatorname{Hom}(G_i,\mathcal Hom(F,H))=\lim_i\operatorname{Hom}(F\otimes G_i,H)$; symmetry gives the other variable. Thus [lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy] applies. It gives $T$, associators by reindexing triple direct sums, and unitors, on complexes and on their homotopy category $K(\mathcal A)$, satisfying pentagon and triangle. The tensor and differential are exactly [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].

source.place: Tag 0FPQ (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes), its unit and diagram hints; total tensor of Section 06YL

proof.text: On a $(p,q)$ summand define $s_{P,N}(x\otimes y)=(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$, using the sheaf symmetry of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. Maps out of a sheaf tensor are determined by their maps on local pure tensors, and maps out of a direct sum by its summands, by the constructions [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Both $d s$ and $s d$ send $x\otimes y$ to $(-1)^{pq}dy\otimes x+(-1)^{pq+q}y\otimes dx$. Hence $s$ is a chain map. Its square has coefficient $(-1)^{pq+qp}=1$, so its inverse is $s_{N,P}$. A pair of degree-zero chain maps does not change $p,q$, proving naturality. This natural isomorphism also acts on the homotopy tensor of step 1: every homotopy-category arrow is a class of chain maps, so the same naturality equality applies to it.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ, commutativity constraints; More on Algebra section-sign-rules

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P$ be the full subcategory of $K(\mathcal A)$ of K-flat complexes with flat terms, as in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. It contains $\mathcal O[0]$: tensor with $\mathcal O$ is the identity, hence $\mathcal O$ is flat by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and [lem-pc-kflat-closure] applies to this bounded-above complex. It is closed under $T$. Indeed for acyclic $B$ and K-flat $P,N$, associativity from step 1 identifies $T(B,T(P,N))$ with $T(T(B,P),N)$; first $T(B,P)$, then the latter tensor, is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For the terms, tensoring with $P^p\otimes N^q$ is a composite of two exact functors, so it is flat. The degree-$n$ term of $T(P,N)$ is a countable sum of such flat sheaves and is flat by [lem-pc-kflat-closure]. All constraints in steps 1 and 2 therefore restrict to $\mathcal P$.

source.place: Tag 07A2 (lemma-tensor-product-K-flat); Section 06YL, bounded-flat-K-flat and tensor construction

proof.text: Use the equivalence $W^{-1}\mathcal P\simeq D(\mathcal O)$ and the bifunctor comparison $QT(P,N)\cong QP\otimes^{\mathbf L}QN$ of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Its natural-transformation extension clause descends the swap of step 2, uniquely, to $\sigma$. It descends the unitors as well (fix one factor to the unit). For the associator use this clause successively in the variables of the two iterated tensor bifunctors: for a third representative $R$, the comparison for $(T(P,N),R)$ is available because step 3 puts $T(P,N)$ in $\mathcal P$. Extend first in two variables, then in the remaining variable. Naturality in the remaining variable holds because its two sides agree on representatives and extension is unique. Equivalently this is the localization universal property of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] applied one variable at a time. Descend the inverse constraints by the same procedure; their inverse identities follow by uniqueness. This constructs the required natural associator, unitors and symmetry on the stated tensor bifunctor.

source.place: Tag 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived), omitted descent expanded using Tags 06YS, 06YU and 0G7D

proof.text: The coherence equations can be checked on K-flat representatives: the localization equivalence makes every tuple of objects isomorphic to such a tuple, and all the constraints are natural. Pentagon and triangle are the images of the identities in [lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy]. The square of the symmetry is the image of the square computed in step 2. For the displayed hexagon, take homogeneous $x\in P^p,y\in N^q,z\in R^r$ in $T(T(P,N),R)$. The left side sends $(x\otimes y)\otimes z$ to $(-1)^{p(q+r)}y\otimes(z\otimes x)$; the right side gives $(-1)^{pq+pr}y\otimes(z\otimes x)$, the same element. The inverse hexagon is checked by moving $z$ past $y,x$, with exponent $r(p+q)=rp+rq$. Swapping past the degree-zero unit has sign one. Equality on local pure-tensor summands gives equality of chain maps as in step 2, hence equality after localization. These are exactly the monoidal axioms of [def-sfb-monoidal-category] and the asserted symmetry identities.

source.place: Tags 0FPQ and 0FPT, coherence verifications; More on Algebra section-sign-rules

proof.text: Check also the one-K-flat representative description in the statement. For a quasi-isomorphism $a:X\to Y$, [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] says $C(a)$ is acyclic. The formulas of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] identify $T(C(a),P)$ with $C(T(a,1_P))$: on $Y^i\otimes P^j$ and $X^{i+1}\otimes P^j$ use the identity after reindexing; the differential on the shifted $X$ summand is $-d_X\otimes1+(-1)^i1\otimes d_P$, the cone differential. If $P$ is K-flat this cone is acyclic, so tensoring with $P$ preserves every quasi-isomorphism. Step 2 gives the other tensor order. If $a$ is a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes, its cone is also K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-closure]; [lem-pur-acyclic-kflat-tensor-arbitrary] makes its tensor with any complex acyclic. Thus changing either representative in a tensor with one K-flat factor gives an invertible localized comparison. Resolve the arbitrary factor and, if needed, resolve the K-flat factor by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The resulting two-flat-term model is the model in step 4. This proves agreement with the tensor specified in the statement, including for K-flat factors without flat terms.

For the closed structure, represent $K,L$ by K-flat flat-term complexes $A,P$, using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and $M$ by a K-injective complex $I$, using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], $H=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I)$ represents $R\mathcal Hom(L,M)$. It is K-injective by [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective]. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] computes morphisms into both $QH$ and $QI$ by homotopy classes of chain maps. These hypotheses require only a small ringed site, as assumed here; no boundedness, constructibility or enough projectives is used.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), representative choices; Tag 0A96 (lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective); Derived Categories Tag 070I

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total] to $A,P,I$. It gives an isomorphism of sheaf complexes $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(A,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I))\cong\mathcal Hom^\bullet(T(A,P),I)$. Apply ordinary global sections termwise and take ordinary $H^0$. By [lem-pur-hom-complex-global-homotopy], the resulting bijection is $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(A,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(T(A,P),I)$. The K-injective comparison from step 7 and the tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] identify this with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(K,R\mathcal Hom(L,M))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}L,M)$. Invert the bijection to obtain the direction displayed in the statement. No identification of ordinary global sections with derived global sections is made.

Make its normalization explicit. By [def-pur-hom-complex] a degree-zero chain map $\varphi:A\to H$ is a family of degree-$p$ graded maps $\varphi(x):P\to I$. Under the sheaf adjunction [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], its uncurrying on the $(p,q)$ summand is $v(x\otimes y)=\varphi(x)(y)\in I^{p+q}$, with no additional sign. The chain-map equation for $\varphi$ is $d_I\varphi(x)-(-1)^p\varphi(x)d_P=\varphi(d_Ax)$, hence $d_Iv(x\otimes y)=v(d_Ax\otimes y)+(-1)^p v(x\otimes d_Py)$. Conversely this equation for all $p,q$ gives the curried chain map. The same formula in degree $-1$ takes a homotopy to a homotopy, because its Hom differential is $d_Ih+hd$. Thus the bijection in step 8 is precisely ordinary evaluation uncurrying on homotopy classes, with the specified total-tensor sign convention.

source.place: Tag 0A90, currying from the definitions of Hom complexes in Section 0A8X and tensor in Section 06YL

proof.text: For chain maps $a:A'\to A$, $b:P'\to P$, $c:I\to I'$ (with $I,I'$ K-injective), the formula in step 9 gives $v'(x'\otimes y')=c(\varphi(a x')(b y'))$. This is both the uncurrying of $\mathcal Hom(b,c)\varphi a$ and the composite $c\,v\,T(a,b)$. The isomorphism [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total] and the global homotopy identification [lem-pur-hom-complex-global-homotopy] are natural, so the equality holds on homotopy classes. Every derived morphism in $K$ and $L$ is obtained from maps between K-flat flat-term representatives and inverses of their quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Naturality squares for these inverse maps follow by inverting the squares for the maps. Every derived morphism in $M$ is a homotopy class of a map between K-injective representatives by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], with such representatives existing by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The Hom functor is the descended one of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Thus the bijection is natural in all three derived variables, contravariantly in $K,L$ and covariantly in $M$.

source.place: Tag 08J9, functoriality; Sections 06YL and 08J7, localization in both tensor variables and the internal Hom

proof.text: For fixed $L$ the natural bijection is an adjunction $-\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\dashv R\mathcal Hom(L,-)$. Define $e_{L,M}$ to be the image of $1_{R\mathcal Hom(L,M)}$ under the inverse transpose. Its chain model is evaluation: with $P,I,H$ as in step 7, choose a K-flat flat-term resolution $t:S\to H$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The identity of $QH$ is represented by $Qt$ after identifying $QS$ with $QH$. Step 9 sends $t$ to $T(S,P)\to I$, $s\otimes y\mapsto t(s)(y)$, precisely resolved evaluation. Naturality in the first variable, established in step 10, applied to $u:K\to R\mathcal Hom(L,M)$ gives $\operatorname{uncurry}(u)=e_{L,M}\circ(u\otimes1_L)$. This identifies the counit and proves the final formula. Together with steps 4 and 5 it proves every clause of the item.
